=== CONTEXT (do NOT extract rows from this part; use only to identify the section headers in effect) ===
e of the 9th inst.,
with respect to the payment of $81.55 to Carroll Haffell Powell to reimburse him for certain expenditures incurred by
him in connection with the sale to him of Little Horse Shoe Island, which sale was subsequently cancelled.

One of the items covered by this payment is a claim of $50 for dynamite purchased by him for the purpose of blasting
a sheltered harbour for a motor boat. I think that this item should be supported by a receipted account or by other
documentary evidence that this amount has been actually expended by Mr. Powell. It does not appear from the
correspondence that the dynamite purchased was actually used at Little Horse Shoe Island. If it were not so used I do
not think that Mr. Powell should be allowed to retain the dynamite in addition to being reimbursed for its purchase.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Payment towards Construction of Provincial Highways

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, June, 23, 1923.

SIR, - Nova Scotia Cheque No. 615, drawn on December 12, 1922, is for the payment of $3,000 to the Town of Truro
as partial cost of reconstructing 3,325 feet of Halifax-Truro highway through Millbrook Indian Reserve.

From a letter from the Town Clerk of Truro, which is attached to the voucher, I infer that this reserve is included in
the Town of Truro, and that the total cost of that part of the road which passes through the reserve was $3,495.

1 - 16 1/2 I



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 594-597) ===
<!-- page 594 -->
It appears to me that although this section of road passes through the Indian reserve it formed a part of the Halifax-
Truro Highway, and as such was constructed or re - Constructed more for the benefit of the public in general and of
the town in particular than for the immediate benefit of the Indians. Under these circumstances would it not have been
more equitable if a greater part of the cost had been borne by the municipality instead of only about one-seventh of the
cost.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, June 26, 1923.

DEAR SIR, - Replying to your letter of June 23 with reference to the highway through the Millbrook Indian Reserve, I
have to inform you that it was the intention of the Department to pay the total cost of constructing the road through the
Indian reserve. This was estimated at $3,000 and when it was completed the cost was $3,495. As $3,000 was the sum
voted by Parliament it was all the Department could pay and the municipality paid the balance.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

The Assistant Auditor General, Ottawa.

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, October 9, 1923

SIR, - Ontario and Quebec Cheque No. 1020, issued on September 13, 1922, is for the payment of $11,987.18 to the
Department of Highways, Province of Quebec, being the "Department's contribution towards the construction of a
portion of the Caughnawaga-Malone Highway through the Caughnawaga Indian Reserve, as per agreement between
the Quebec Provincial Government and this Department, dated January, 1920."

In connection with this payment I have to ask for a copy of the agreement entered into between your Department and
the Provincial Government, together with copies of any correspondence you may have had in connection with this
payment. Was the agreement referred to above approved by the Governor-in-Council?

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

<!-- page 595 -->
DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, October 22, 1923.

DEAR SIR, - I am in receipt of your letter of October 9, asking that a copy of the agreement entered into between this
Department, and the Quebec Provincial Government in connection with the amount which was to be contributed by
this Department towards the construction of a portion of the Caughnawaga-Malone Highway, through the
Caughnawaga Indian Reserve be sent to you.

In reply, I beg to say that there was no special agreement executed, other than the correspondence between this
Department, the Provincial Government and the Dominion Highway Commission, copies of which are enclosed
herewith for your information together with copies of correspondence in connection with the payment of the above
mentioned expenditure.

As you will note it was first intended that this grant be paid from the funds at the credit of the Caughnawaga Indians,
but it was later considered inadvisable as this course would have depleted the funds of this band to a much greater
extent than that anticipated when the first estimates were being submitted by the Quebec Provincial Government.
Provision to meet this expenditure was therefore made in the Supplementary Estimates of 1922 - 23.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

The Assistant Auditor General, Ottawa.

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, October 30, 1923.

SIR, - I am in receipt of your letter of the 22nd inst. (No. 23005) with enclosures, in reply to mine of the 9th, regarding
a payment to the Quebec Department of Highways of $11,987.18 being your department's contribution towards the
construction of that portion of the Caughnawaga-Malone Highway which passes through the Caughnawaga Reserve.

The plan adopted in this case of basing your contribution on the actual, necessary and reasonable cost as established by
the Highways Commission, instead of on the actual amount paid out by the Quebec Government is, in my opinion, the
correct one. I am of opinion however, that this payment and all payments of a similar nature should be authorized by
the Governor-in-Council, and have accordingly to request you to obtain the authority of Council for the same.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

NOTE. - An Order in Council was passed on December 17, 1923, authorizing the above payment.

AUDIT OFFICE, OCTOBER 9, 1923.

SIR, - Ontario and Quebec cheque No. 869, issued on August 25th, 1922, is for the payment of $12,814.42 to the
Ontario Department of Public High-

ways in settlement of your department's share of the expenditure on the Provincial Highway through the Tyendinaga

This payment is made up as follows: -

                                                                                                               ...
$42,478.43.

Total paid by Department                                                                                       $12,814 42

In connection with this payment, I have to ask if any agreement was entered into between the Provincial Government
and your Department, with regard to the division of the costs of this road; if any such agreement was made, kindly let
me have a copy of the same.

I notice that in this case your department is charged with 30 per cent of the cost of construction for the first year, and
with 20 per cent of the combined cost of construction and cost of maintenance for the second year, the amounts paid
being based on the figures supplied by the Provincial Engineer of Highways. In the case of a similar payment to the
Quebec Provincial Government for a contribution to the Caughnawaga-Malone Highway, through the Caughnawaga
Reserve, the amount paid by your department was only 10 per cent, and that 10 per cent was based not on the amount
of $181,000 to be paid to the contractor, but on $122,371.80, the amount arrived at by the Dominion Highways
Commissioner as being the strictly necessary expenditure under the Canadian Highways Act and regulations
thereunder. I should like to be advised as to why the payment to the Ontario Provincial Government was treated in a
different manner from that to the Quebec Provincial Government.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.
DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, October 11, 1923.

SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 9th instant, respecting a payment of $12,814.42 to the Ontario Department of Public
Highways in settlement of this Department's share of the expenditure on the Provincial Highway through the
Tyendinaga Indian Reserve; I beg to enclose a copy of a letter dated 15th November, 1921, from the Department of
Public Highways for the Province of Ontario which will afford you the information you require.

Your obedient servant,
J.D. McLEAN, Asst. Deputy and Secretary.

The Assistant Auditor General, Ottawa.

<!-- page 597 -->
DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HIGHWAYS, TORONTO, November 15, 1921.

DEAR SIR, - The Provincial Highway easterly from Toronto to Ottawa and the Quebec boundary passes through the
southern portion of the County of Hastings. A portion of this highway from approximately the village of Marysville to
the town of Deseronto, passes through the Tyendinaga Indian Reserve; also a short section in the vicinity of
Shannonville.

Under the Provincial Highway Act a portion of all expenditure on Provincial Highways within the County is
chargeable to the corporation of the county. For the year 1919 this proportion was thirty per cent of the expenditure,
and for the year 1920 the proportion was twenty per cent.

The County of Hastings, in making payment of the amount levied upon the county, have objected to being held
responsible for expenditure within the Indian Reserve; and I am recently advised by Mr. Robert Cook, M.P.P., that
upon representations made to the Department of Indian Affairs, your Department has consented to relieve the County
of Hastings from liability for expenditure within the Indian Reserve.

Upon the advice of Mr. Cook, I am therefore enclosing to you statements of our expenditure for the years in question.
As shown by the summary accompanying the statements for the two years, the amount of $4,318.73 is due on account
of expenditure in the year 1919; and $8,495.69 for expenditure in the year 1920.

I would be pleased to receive from you confirmation of our understanding in the matter, that your Department will
assume the obligation of the county of Hastings with respect to the Provincial Highway in the Tyendinaga Indian
Reserve.

A copy of the Provincial Highway Act and amendments thereto is herewith enclosed.

Yours truly,
(Sgd.) W.A. McLEAN.
AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, October 29, 1923.

SIR - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 11th inst., (No. 23034 - 2) in reply to mine of the 9th inst.,
respecting a payment of $12,814.42 to the Ontario Department of Public Highways in connection with the Highway
through the Tyendinaga Indian Reserve.

It appears from your reply that under the Provincial Highways Act a portion of all expenditure on Provincial Highways
within any county is chargeable against the corporation of that county, and that the proportions so chargeable were
fixed at 30 per cent of the expenditure for 1919 and 20 per cent for 1920. It further appears that the county of Hastings
objected to being held responsible for expenditure within the Indian Reserve and that accordingly your department
agreed to relieve the county from liability for such expenditure.

The amount paid by you to the Province of Ontario on account of construction was $12,589.32 being 30 per cent of
$14,395.78 for 1919, and 20 per cent of $41,352.93 for 1920, and $225.10 on account of maintenance for 1920 being
20 per cent of $1,125.50.

I beg to point out that the Department of Railways and Canals had already paid to the Province of Ontario the sum of
$16,168.29, being 40 per cent of $40,420.72 the amount established by the Highways Commission as being the actual,
necessary and reasonable cost to December 31, 1920, of the Highway through the Tyendinaga Reserve.
